question: Should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 define the shared public reaction-wake contract, or should OpenClaw use channel-specific or per-message awaiting semantics instead?
rationale: The alternatives create materially different config, persistence, plugin-ownership, parity, and upgrade commitments that source inspection cannot resolve without maintainer intent.

options.title: Shared default-off policy
options.body: Define one notification wake contract and have each bundled channel apply it after existing ingress filters.

options.title: Channel-specific policies
options.body: Allow plugins to expose independent wake settings, accepting configuration drift and uneven cross-channel behavior.

options.title: Per-message awaiting state
options.body: Wake only for explicitly marked outbound messages, requiring durable message-state and lifecycle design first.

recommendation.title: Shared default-off policy
recommendation.body: Define one notification wake contract and have each bundled channel apply it after existing ingress filters.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review explicitly routed this public product/API choice to maintainer follow-up and kept this issue canonical.
